ARABIC LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #20
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ARABIC LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What does the Arabic word كَيْفَ حَالُكَ؟ (kayfa haaluka?) mean? (1 mark)
   A. How are you? (to a boy)
   B. and upon you peace (the reply)
   C. welcome
   D. I

2. Which Arabic word means "I am well"? (1 mark)
   A. مَعَ السَّلَامَةِ
   B. اسْمِي
   C. مَرْحَبًا
   D. أَنَا بِخَيْرٍ

3. What does the Arabic sentence أَخِي يَلْعَبُ mean? (1 mark)
   A. This is my mother.
   B. I have a brother and a sister.
   C. My brother plays.
   D. This is my father.

4. What does the Arabic sentence أُخْتِي تَقْرَأُ mean? (1 mark)
   A. My sister reads.
   B. I have a brother and a sister.
   C. This is my father.
   D. This is my mother.

5. What does the Arabic word أَبٌ (ab) mean? (1 mark)
   A. mother's brother
   B. father's brother
   C. sister
   D. father

6. What does the Arabic sentence الْكِتَابُ عَلَى الطَّاوِلَةِ mean? (1 mark)
   A. The lamp is above the table.
   B. The cat is under the bed.
   C. The pen is in the bag.
   D. The book is on the table.

7. Which Arabic instruction means 'sit down'? (1 mark)
   A. qif
   B. iqraʾ
   C. ukhruj
   D. ijlis

8. How is the Arabic word اُخْرُجْ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. ukhruj
   B. iftahi l-baab
   C. uktub
   D. aghliqi l-baab

9. What does the Arabic sentence أَلْعَبُ يَوْمَ السَّبْتِ mean? (1 mark)
   A. Today is Thursday.
   B. There are seven days in a week.
   C. I go to school on Monday.
   D. I play on Saturday.

10. What does the Arabic word طَعَامٌ (taʿaam) mean? (1 mark)
   A. birthday
   B. food
   C. please, go ahead
   D. friend

11. Which sentence means 'Do you like bananas?' (1 mark)
   A. hal tuhibbu l-mawz?
   B. ashrabu l-mawz
   C. aakulu l-mawz
   D. uhibbu l-mawz

12. What does the Arabic sentence أَشُمُّ بِأَنْفِي mean? (1 mark)
   A. I hear with my ear.
   B. I speak with my mouth.
   C. I see with my eye.
   D. I smell with my nose.

13. What is intonation? (1 mark)
   A. The number of words
   B. The size of letters
   C. The rise and fall of the voice when speaking
   D. The speed of writing

14. What does the Arabic word رِيحٌ (riih) mean? (1 mark)
   A. environment
   B. cold
   C. wind
   D. beautiful

15. What are the three parts of a short speech? (1 mark)
   A. Question, answer and test
   B. Opening, middle and closing
   C. Song, dance and drum
   D. Title, picture and page

16. How do you read the syllable بِ? (1 mark)
   A. bi
   B. nu
   C. tu
   D. bii

17. What is the name of the Arabic letter ذ? (1 mark)
   A. dhaal
   B. thaa
   C. daal
   D. laam

18. What is the name of the Arabic letter ا? (1 mark)
   A. daal
   B. nuun
   C. Saad
   D. alif

19. How do you read the syllable سُ? (1 mark)
   A. laa
   B. bu
   C. na
   D. su

20. What does the word يَا (yaa) do in مَرْحَبًا يَا أَحْمَدُ? (1 mark)
   A. It calls a person, like 'O' or 'hey'
   B. It means 'in'
   C. It means 'my'
   D. It means 'and'

21. How do you read the shadda in the word jad-dun? (1 mark)
   A. The word is a question
   B. The vowel is long
   C. The letter daal is said twice
   D. The letter is silent

22. What is the theme of a text? (1 mark)
   A. Its number of lines
   B. Its main topic
   C. Its colour
   D. Its size

23. Which Arabic sentence means "The house is big." (1 mark)
   A. فِي الْمَطْبَخِ طَاوِلَةٌ وَكُرْسِيٌّ
   B. أَزْرَعُ شَجَرَةً
   C. عَلَى الطَّاوِلَةِ كُوبٌ
   D. الْبَيْتُ كَبِيرٌ

24. Which Arabic word means "food"? (1 mark)
   A. تَفَضَّلْ
   B. شَمْعَةٌ
   C. بَالُونٌ
   D. طَعَامٌ

25. Which Arabic word means "bread"? (1 mark)
   A. خُبْزٌ
   B. سُكَّرٌ
   C. طَمَاطِمُ
   D. تُفَّاحٌ

26. What does jism mean? (1 mark)
   A. head
   B. hand
   C. body
   D. heart

27. Which of these Arabic words (in English letters) means 'clouds'? (1 mark)
   A. matar
   B. ghaym
   C. shams
   D. riih

28. What does the word min mean in maTaru mina s-samaa'i? (1 mark)
   A. from
   B. in
   C. and
   D. on

29. What does the Arabic sentence الْمِفْتَاحُ فِي الْخِزَانَةِ mean? (1 mark)
   A. The key is in the cupboard.
   B. Do not play with the knife.
   C. I read a book on Sunday.
   D. The chair is at the door.

30. What does al-miftaahu fii l-khizaana mean? (1 mark)
   A. The chair is at the door.
   B. The pen is in the bag.
   C. The key is in the cupboard.
   D. The lamp is above the table.

31. What is the name of the Arabic letter ص? (1 mark)
   A. Taa
   B. Saad
   C. ghayn
   D. nuun

32. Which sound does the Arabic letter ر make? (1 mark)
   A. th as in think
   B. b as in bag
   C. a quick rolled r
   D. l as in lamp

33. Which of these letters does NOT join to the letter after it? (1 mark)
   A. ر (raa)
   B. ب (baa)
   C. ن (nuun)
   D. س (siin)

34. How is the Arabic word حَقِيبَةٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. miftaah
   B. haqiiba
   C. hammaam
   D. bayt

35. Which letter is missing in الجم_ة? (1 mark)
   A. ف (faa)
   B. ح (Haa)
   C. غ (ghayn)
   D. ع (ʿayn)

36. What does the Arabic sentence نَحْنُ نَرْقُصُ mean? (1 mark)
   A. My mother cooks the food.
   B. I have a gift.
   C. I like the party.
   D. We dance.

37. Which Arabic word means "my turn"? (1 mark)
   A. صَدِيقٌ
   B. دَوْرِي
   C. عِيدٌ
   D. بَالُونٌ

38. What does the Arabic word سُكَّرٌ (sukkar) mean? (1 mark)
   A. carrots
   B. bread
   C. milk
   D. sugar

39. How does rain help people? (1 mark)
   A. It makes crops die
   B. It stops all farming
   C. It helps crops to grow and gives us water
   D. It has no use

40. What does the Arabic sentence فِي الْغُرْفَةِ سَرِيرٌ mean? (1 mark)
   A. I like my house.
   B. In the kitchen there is a table.
   C. This is my room.
   D. In the room there is a bed.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Translate into English: al-kitaabu ʿalaa t-taawila (2 marks)

42. Explain why poems help us when learning a language. (2 marks) (2 marks)

43. Describe how to solve a jumbled sentence. (3 marks) (3 marks)

44. Explain what it means to read with fluency and give two tips for reading fluently. (3 marks) (3 marks)

45. Translate into English: hadiyya li-Aminata (2 marks)

46. Write three instructions about the body in Arabic sounds with meanings. (3 marks) (3 marks)

47. Explain how a family celebration you know helps people to live together in peace. (3 marks) (3 marks)

48. Translate into English: haadhihi yadii (2 marks)

49. Write the Arabic sounds for 'two hands' and 'two legs' and give the meaning of each ending. (3 marks) (3 marks)

50. Translate into English: akhii Sagiir (2 marks)

51. Translate into English: ayna l-kitaab? (2 marks)

52. Put the words in order and translate: كَبِيرٌ / بَيْتِي. (2 marks) (2 marks)

53. Translate into English: ummii tatbukhu (2 marks)

54. Give three ways of taking care of your body. (3 marks) (3 marks)

55. Translate into English: aakulu l-aruzza (2 marks)

56. Give three tips for neat handwriting with good word spacing. (3 marks) (3 marks)

57. Give three tips that help a speaker to use tone and pace well. (3 marks) (3 marks)

58. Write one Arabic sentence about your body in sounds and translate it. (2 marks) (2 marks)

59. Translate into English: ar-riihu qawiyya (2 marks)

60. Explain the three reading strategies: decoding, cues and word spacing. (3 marks) (3 marks)

61. Translate into English: al-kursiyyu jadiid (2 marks)

62. Translate into English: fii l-matbakhi taawila wa kursii (2 marks)

63. Translate into English: ash-shamsu fii s-samaa'i (2 marks)

64. Translate into English: haadhaa raʾsii (2 marks)

65. Describe three ways to work out the meaning of an unfamiliar word. (3 marks) (3 marks)
pages.answers:
ARABIC LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #20 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — How are you? (to a boy)
   كَيْفَ حَالُكَ؟ (kayfa haaluka?) means How are you? (to a boy).

2. D — أَنَا بِخَيْرٍ
   أَنَا بِخَيْرٍ (anaa bi-khayr) means I am well.

3. C — My brother plays.
   أَخِي يَلْعَبُ (akhii yalʿabu) means: My brother plays.

4. A — My sister reads.
   أُخْتِي تَقْرَأُ (ukhtii taqraʾu) means: My sister reads.

5. D — father
   أَبٌ (ab) means father.

6. D — The book is on the table.
   الْكِتَابُ عَلَى الطَّاوِلَةِ (al-kitaabu ʿalaa t-taawila) means: The book is on the table.

7. D — ijlis
   ijlis means sit down. qif means stand up.

8. A — ukhruj
   اُخْرُجْ is read ukhruj and means go out.

9. D — I play on Saturday.
   أَلْعَبُ يَوْمَ السَّبْتِ (alʿabu yawma s-sabt) means: I play on Saturday.

10. B — food
   طَعَامٌ (taʿaam) means food.

11. A — hal tuhibbu l-mawz?
   hal makes a question and tuhibbu means 'you like'.

12. D — I smell with my nose.
   أَشُمُّ بِأَنْفِي (ashummu bi-anfii) means: I smell with my nose.

13. C — The rise and fall of the voice when speaking
   Intonation is how the voice goes up and down.

14. C — wind
   رِيحٌ (riih) means wind.

15. B — Opening, middle and closing
   A speech opens by greeting, gives the main information and closes by thanking.

16. A — bi
   بِ is read bi.

17. A — dhaal
   The letter ذ is called dhaal.

18. D — alif
   The letter ا is called alif.

19. D — su
   سُ is read su.

20. A — It calls a person, like 'O' or 'hey'
   yaa is used to call someone by name.

21. C — The letter daal is said twice
   A shadda doubles the letter, so jadd has two d sounds.

22. B — Its main topic
   The theme is the main subject of the text.

23. D — الْبَيْتُ كَبِيرٌ
   الْبَيْتُ كَبِيرٌ (al-baytu kabiir) means: The house is big.

24. D — طَعَامٌ
   طَعَامٌ (taʿaam) means food.

25. A — خُبْزٌ
   خُبْزٌ (khubz) means bread.

26. C — body
   jism means body.

27. B — ghaym
   ghaym means clouds.

28. A — from
   min means 'from', so 'the rain is from the sky'.

29. A — The key is in the cupboard.
   الْمِفْتَاحُ فِي الْخِزَانَةِ (al-miftaahu fii l-khizaana) means: The key is in the cupboard.

30. C — The key is in the cupboard.
   miftaah is key and khizaana is cupboard.

31. B — Saad
   The letter ص is called Saad.

32. C — a quick rolled r
   The letter ر makes the sound a quick rolled r.

33. A — ر (raa)
   raa joins only to the letter before it. So do alif, daal, dhaal, zaay and waaw.

34. B — haqiiba
   حَقِيبَةٌ is read haqiiba and means bag.

35. D — ع (ʿayn)
   The word is الجمعة, al-jumuʿa, Friday.

36. D — We dance.
   نَحْنُ نَرْقُصُ (nahnu narqusu) means: We dance.

37. B — دَوْرِي
   دَوْرِي (dawrii) means my turn.

38. D — sugar
   سُكَّرٌ (sukkar) means sugar.

39. C — It helps crops to grow and gives us water
   Rain waters crops and fills rivers and tanks.

40. D — In the room there is a bed.
   فِي الْغُرْفَةِ سَرِيرٌ (fii l-ghurfati sariir) means: In the room there is a bed.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: The book is on the table.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: The rhythm and rhyme help us to remember words and to practise pronunciation.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for memory and 1 mark for pronunciation.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Find the word that names the item; find the position or describing word; put them together in the pattern and read aloud to check.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Fluency means reading smoothly at a steady speed with correct words. Tips: put a finger under each word; practise at slow and normal speed.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning and 1 mark for each tip.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: A gift for Amina.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: irfaʿ yadaka (raise your hand), ilmis anfaka (touch your nose), aghmiD ʿaynayka (close your eyes).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct instruction with meaning.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: People meet, share food and joy, sing and talk together, and learn to respect one another.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meeting, 1 mark for sharing, 1 mark for respect.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: This is my hand.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: yadaani (two hands) and rijlaani (two legs). The ending -aani means two.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each word and 1 mark for the ending.

50. (2 marks)
   Answer: My brother is small.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: Where is the book?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: بَيْتِي كَبِيرٌ. My house is big.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the order and 1 mark for the translation.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: My mother cooks.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Wash hands and face; clean teeth; eat good food; sleep well; play outdoors.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid way.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: I eat rice.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Leave a gap about one letter wide between words; keep letters in a word joined smoothly; write on the baseline; put dots neatly.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid tip.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: Speak loudly enough and clearly; speak at a steady speed; pause between sentences; smile when greeting.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid tip.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example aktubu bi-yadii. I write with my hand.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a correct sentence and 1 mark for the translation.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: The wind is strong.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

60. (3 marks)
   Answer: Decoding: sounding out each letter and mark. Cues: using pictures and the sentence to guess. Word spacing: looking at the spaces to see where words begin and end.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each strategy.

61. (2 marks)
   Answer: The chair is new.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

62. (2 marks)
   Answer: In the kitchen there is a table and a chair.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

63. (2 marks)
   Answer: The sun is in the sky.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

64. (2 marks)
   Answer: This is my head.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

65. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use the sentence around the word; use a picture or a word you know; look it up in a dictionary or ask.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.
